body: About · undrwrld_rcrds About undrwrld_rcrds An editorial layer for the underground dance scene that mostly doesn't have one — covering angelcore, aero, outsider house, and the broader post-club electronic landscape. by undrwrld_rcrds ∙ About undrwrld_rcrds is a one-person music publication writing about the contemporary underground dance scene. The core focus is the cluster of microgenres that emerged out of the late-2010s SoundCloud underground and consolidated into recognizable scenes through 2024 and 2025 — angelcore, aero, outsider house, and the broader post-club electronic landscape that surrounds them. Adjacent material — witch house, dreampop, lo-fi house, the y2k-recombinant edges of contemporary pop — gets covered where it intersects with the core focus. Why This Exists Most music journalism is structured around bands and records that already have publicists, label support, and reliable touring revenue. The scenes covered here mostly don't. Angelcore's working canon emerged through Spotify recommendation, YouTube playlist curation, and TikTok video uses rather than through editorial press; aero is even newer, and most of what gets written about it lives on Album of the Year user reviews and Discord servers; outsider house has, since the late 2010s, been one of the most under-covered electronic scenes relative to its catalog quality. None of these scenes need a publication; all of them benefit from one existing. undrwrld_rcrds is the project working from that premise. The editorial approach is straightforward: long-form profiles, structurally-attentive reviews, scene-history essays, and the kind of context-setting that algorithmic playlist discovery cannot provide. Writeups are research-driven and verified against publicly documented information; when a fact can't be verified, the writeup works around the gap rather than inventing detail. Coverage skews toward established and emerging producers operating in the scenes' canonical and satellite tiers rather than toward strict newness for its own sake. Scope What gets covered here, in rough order of focus: Angelcore. The post-witch-house, post-club electronic scene that consolidated around 2024. Coverage includes the canonical producers, the satellite tier, the label and curatorial infrastructure (Azurite Records, EPSILE, ARCADIA / IMMINENT, and the broader independent-label ecosystem), and the scene's individual canonical tracks. Aero. The y2k-recombinant strain of underground house that crystallized around yaego's 2025 ÆRO EP. Coverage includes the founding producers (yaego, wzrdd, skrta), the scene's working aesthetic, and individual track reviews. Outsider house. The lo-fi, analogue-leaning offshoot of house music born in the early 2010s. Coverage is more historical and includes producers like Cult Member alongside the contemporary scene's connective tissue to angelcore. Adjacent material. Witch-house lineage records that inform the contemporary sound; dreampop-leaning angelcore satellite work; specific releases from outside these scenes that get pulled into their orbit through curation. How Coverage Works Profiles, reviews, and essays are written from publicly available information, listening to the catalogs, and the kind of context that emerges from being inside the scene's playlist and curation graph. Writeups attempt to be honest about what is verified and what isn't — when a producer's biographical background isn't publicly documented, the writeup says so rather than inventing it. Cross-linking is dense by design; the scenes covered here function as connected ecosystems rather than as isolated artists, and the editorial structure reflects that. The publication is not affiliated with any of the labels, collectives, or playlists it covers. It is also not affiliated with any of the producers whose work it discusses, including those whose work has been positively reviewed. Contact For tips, corrections, demos, or general correspondence: undrwrld.rcrds@gmail.com Demos are welcome but the publication is small and not every submission gets covered. Producers operating in the scenes listed above are more likely to get a response than those outside them. Direct, specific pitches do better than mass outreach. Corrections are taken seriously. If something in a writeup is factually wrong, send the correction with a verifiable source and it will be updated promptly. — Start here: what is angelcore , what is aero , a primer on outsider house .

body: Field Guide · 04 January 2026 · 22 min read Twenty Artists Defining the Angelcore / Aero Continuum in 2026 From the LONOWN / akiaura working partnership to the yaego / wzrdd aero project, plus the satellite producers populating ARCADIA's playlists — a working list of the names worth knowing as the scene crystallizes. by undrwrld_rcrds ∙ Artists The angelcore / aero / outsider house cluster is small enough that a list of its most important producers is actually feasible. What follows is not a strict ranking — the genre is too internally varied for that to mean much — but a working roll call of the artists whose work has shaped the sound's current iteration, drawn from compilation lineups, editorial playlist regulars, and the producers other producers in the scene consistently cite. akiaura saint petersburg · angelcore / witch house The single most consequential producer in the contemporary angelcore lineage. Coming up through the corecore and witch-house-adjacent SoundCloud underground, akiaura broke through with the 2023 EP Ketamine Girl and the viral single Sleepwalker — which across its various slowed and remixed versions has accumulated something on the order of 288 million Spotify streams and 600M+ TikTok video uses. Start with Ketamine Girl , then the LONOWN-collaborative Destruction Age (2024) for the album-length statement. Spotify · 3.3M monthly listeners Sleepwalker (182M streams) akiaura · 2023 listen LONOWN russia · angelcore akiaura's most frequent collaborator and the co-architect of the angelcore sound. The pair's 2024 album Destruction Age is the genre's foundational text; LONOWN's solo tracks ( starly , plus the broader catalog across the scene's release ecosystem) are at the more rhythmically intact end of the spectrum and tend to sit at the front of any contemporary angelcore mixtape. Functions as the genre's compositional anchor. Spotify · 6.7M monthly listeners AVANGARD (107M streams) LONOWN · 2024 listen yaego prince george's county, md · aero / electroclash The pioneer of aero and the producer responsible for crystallizing the y2k-recombinant sound as a coherent aesthetic project. The 2025 EP ÆRO is the genre's foundational document; the broader catalog ( EUROPA , The Sensation , TKOHHH , the Ketamina collaboration with KUČKA) maps the project's range. Visual presence on TikTok is unusually controlled for the scene — slow-motion strobe lights, overexposed-and-undersaturated photography, an abstract futurism filtered through y2k iconography — and the music sounds like the natural soundtrack to that visual world. Spotify · 491K monthly listeners Fe en Rebelión (2.7M) yaego · 2025 listen wzrdd undisclosed · aero yaego's most frequent collaborator and arguably aero's co-author. aerotheworld , ill watch you burn us , and the broader Yaego & wzrdd discography form the genre's connective tissue. wzrdd's solo work runs the same recombinant playbook with a slightly harder rhythmic core. Worth tracking independently of the yaego collaborations. Spotify · aero collaborator aerotheworld (w/ yaego) wzrdd · 2025 listen skrta toronto · aero / trance-leaning The third member of the aero founding triad, sitting closer to the genre's trance-derived edge. The Yaego & skrta collaboration iseeghosts! [waitaminute] is one of the more rhythmically intact entries in the aero canon and a useful demonstration of how trance lineage gets metabolized into the broader project. Spotify · aero / trance edge iseeghosts! [waitaminute] skrta · 2024 listen DJ Anemia russia · angelcore / curator Operates simultaneously as producer and curator. The ANGELCORE PLAYLIST mixtape series — particularly the DJ Anemia & crier collaborative volumes — has functioned as the scene's most consistent editorial document outside of the broader canonical apparatus release calendar. Tracks tend toward the more dissolved end of the genre spectrum, leaning closer to ambient than to dance music proper. Spotify · angelcore curator archangel DJ Anemia · 2024 listen crier undisclosed · angelcore Frequent DJ Anemia collaborator and an increasingly visible producer in their own right. The DJ Anemia / Crier / sixnite track with you is a useful entry point. Production is more melodically forward than most of the scene — the vocal hooks land harder, the patience is less pronounced. Spotify · DJ Anemia collaborator with you (w/ sixnite) crier · 2025 listen angelrot bay area, ca · multi-genre electronic One of the more visible Bay Area producers operating in the broader angelcore / opiumcore space, with roughly 100,000 monthly Spotify listeners and a presence on the "Angelcore: Compiled" compilation. The catalog is unusually broad for a scene this niche — Soft Collapse (2025) functions as the most fully realized album-length statement, while singles like iconic , STAYWITHME , and eurosummer (all 2026) demonstrate the producer's willingness to move between the genre's softer and more uptempo poles. Self-described as multi-genre, which reads accurately: tracks like Never Me sit closer to dreampop, while tonic moves into harder territory. A useful contemporary single-artist entry point for a listener trying to get oriented in the current scene. Spotify · 104K monthly listeners iconic angelrot · 2026 listen Baby Jane los angeles · gothic house / angelcore-adjacent Sofia Bella Galuz — born 2001, based in Los Angeles, singer-songwriter and producer working in a self-described "gothic house" register that fuses witch house, hardstyle, and ethereal pop. Featured on the canonical Deathwish track alongside akiaura and LONOWN. Operates at the more vocally-forward end of angelcore — the lyric is more present, the song more legible as a song, even as the surrounding production stays well inside genre conventions. A useful entry point for listeners coming to angelcore from a more traditional pop or alt-pop background. Spotify · gothic house / LA A Grave Marked Strange Baby Jane · 2025 listen VNXIOUS undisclosed · angelcore One of the scene's most prolific producers and one of its most reliable curators — the prodvnxious-tagged YouTube angelcore mixes are a parallel canon to the established editorial center playlists. Solo tracks lean toward the more compressed and immediate end of the genre; the release cadence alone has made VNXIOUS a fixture on every relevant playlist. Hugeloud undisclosed · angelcore / electroclash One of the bigger names you haven't heard of yet — 314K monthly listeners on Spotify, top track Destiny sitting at 2.8 million streams, and the kind of catalog depth that signals a producer who's been working this register since before it had a name. The 2026 release calendar — Empty streets , Subtle Attack , Dancefloor , Jumpstyle 2006 — pulls in jumpstyle, dirty electro house, and the kind of cosmic-club register that bridges angelcore's more melodic side to the broader contemporary dance ecology. BURN FOR YOU and its slowed edition together cleared 4 million streams. The project's been on the official Angelcore Spotify playlist since the playlist had room for anyone. Spotify · 314.5K monthly listeners Destiny (2.8M streams) Hugeloud · 2023 listen Kaikobad undisclosed · outsider house / lo-fi 427K monthly listeners and a top track — Turn Echo — sitting at 7.1 million streams. The catalog reads as outsider house executed at the more melodic, listener-friendly end of the lineage; the Cult Member Archive, wiv, and Gygas adjacencies on the Spotify recommendation graph put Kaikobad squarely in the contemporary outsider house cohort even when individual tracks lean closer to ambient or downtempo. The Turn Echo (Slowed Version) at 2.1M streams demonstrates the parallel-version distribution model working at scale in the outsider house corner too — not just angelcore. Spotify · 427.7K monthly listeners Turn Echo (7.1M streams) Kaikobad · 2025 listen XEOE undisclosed · aero / hardwave Pronounced shay-oh. 1.1 million monthly listeners and a catalog whose top track — TRIPPLEX - Ultra Slowed — has crossed 15.5 million streams. The project sits at the louder, harder edge of the aero adjacency, with BRUTAL at 8.4M and EGO - SUPER SLOWED at 5M. Recent release Angel Radio 2 (early 2026) makes the angelcore-adjacent positioning explicit; the rest of the catalog is more hardwave-coded but operates in the same emotional register. By raw streaming numbers, one of the largest individual artists in the entire scene-adjacent space. The 2026 release cadence is fast — Core4 , Aireco , Melithe , Cordurance , Glass life , So close all dropped within months of each other — and the project keeps a presence on the Hardwave Task Force compilation track listing alongside the dedicated angelcore curations. Listed contact is cnqrmusic@gmail.com if you're trying to reach the project directly. Spotify · 101.8K monthly listeners In your soul (938K streams) CNQR+ · 2025 listen The Dark Architect undisclosed · dark minimal house Smaller numbers, denser project — 10K monthly listeners, but five full albums ( THE SORROWS OF OUR NATURE , RATHER BE FEARED, THAN LOVED , DAYS AFTER DEATH , PARKING GARAGE ANGELS , The Dark Side of Intimacy ) and a release rhythm that doesn't look like most working producers'. Top track PISCEAN BLOOD at 131K. The aesthetic is dark minimal house — slow, sparse, mostly mid-tempo, with album titles and track titles ( SAGITTARIUS LILITH , IS THIS THE DEMON YOU SENT? , SANRIO LUVS CIGARETTES ) that do a lot of the emotional framing before the first kick lands. Producer's own framing per the bio: "my music contains pieces of my soul, the deepest places of my emotional state." Take that or leave it — the project sits at the genuinely-underground end of the spectrum, and the catalog rewards the patience. Spotify · 10.1K monthly listeners PISCEAN BLOOD (131K streams) The Dark Architect · 2025 listen Gygas undisclosed · angelcore / outsider house — ARCADIA / IMMINENT Per the Spotify bio: "label: ARCADIA / IMMINENT." The project operates across multiple registers — straight angelcore, outsider house, the GHG NIGHTDRIVE / Rally House playlist circuit — but the through-line is a kind of patient vibe-construction that resists easy categorization. Going to be one of the more interesting trajectories to watch as ARCADIA / IMMINENT keeps building out its roster beyond the canonical names. Spotify · 192.4K monthly listeners Loveless (1.16M streams) Gygas · 2024 listen wiv undisclosed · outsider house / lo-fi house One of the largest individual artists in the broader outsider house ecosystem — 1.37 million monthly listeners, top track i love u. at 24.8 million streams, the slowed edition another 12.9 million on top. Released the clarity collaboration with Crisys on Cresta La Cultura in 2026. Producer's own framing per the bio is "emotional experiment" rendered in old-english script, which fits — the catalog operates at the more melodically forward, vocally legible end of angelcore, with the 2025 album Virtual Love as the project's clearest album-length statement so far. A Primer on the Lo-fi House Underground A primer on the lo-fi, analogue-leaning offshoot of house music that was born in the early 2010s as a counter to the mainstream's polish — and that has quietly informed everything from contemporary angelcore to the current SoundCloud rip-and-flip economy. by undrwrld_rcrds ∙ Field Notes Outsider house is a form of house music characterized by its intentional use of rough, lo-fi production, often built from a mix of analogue or analogue-modeled gear and digital instrumentation. Born in the early 2010s, the genre has been analyzed as a movement standing in deliberate opposition to the commercialization trends that defined mainstream house through that same period — sidestepping the polished production, surgical mixing, and EDM-festival arrangements that had come to define the genre at scale. Though it draws most of its DNA from the soulful, laid-back styles of 1990s and 2000s deep house, outsider house also re-contextualizes and borrows from a broader pool of electronic dance music outside its immediate sphere: various 1990s techno genres, ambient house, and the more exploratory edges of the broader EDM canon. It is, in short, what house music sounds like when nobody is trying to make a floor-filler — and when the producer would rather sound like a tape that's been left in a basement than a track that's been mastered for a stadium. body: Roundup · 06 November 2025 · 8 min read The Satellite Tier: Five Producers Defining the Angelcore Middle Ground A working roundup of the producers in the next tier down from the canonical akiaura / LONOWN / DJ Anemia axis — collaborators, release-calendar populators, and the working middle ground of the contemporary scene. by undrwrld_rcrds ∙ Roundup Most of the working coverage of the angelcore scene focuses on the canonical center — the akiaura / LONOWN axis, the DJ Anemia / crier curatorial apparatus, the ARCADIA / IMMINENT release calendar — and on the genre's most-streamed individual tracks. This is reasonable; that's where the gravitational center is. But it leaves out the producers doing the structural work that lets the scene function as a working ecosystem rather than as a small group of canonical names plus everyone else. The five producers in this roundup operate in what is fairly described as the scene's working middle — between the genre's canonical center (akiaura, LONOWN, DJ Anemia) and the broader long tail of producers working at sub-10K monthly listeners. They mostly know each other, collaborate constantly, populate the same playlists, and together produce more of the genre's working release calendar than the canonical tier does. If you're trying to actually listen to the scene rather than just hear its hits, this is where most of the hours go. ProdChxn — 72K monthly listeners ProdChxn is, by collaboration density alone, the broader producer pool's most central figure. The producer's top track — Devotion , at 565,943 plays — is a three-way collaboration with Crisys and Krembuur , and that's the structural pattern the rest of the catalog runs on. Most of the high-streaming ProdChxn tracks are collaborations: Citadelle with Crisys, LUSTER with Crisys, Featherfall as a solo release with strong cross-listing into the broader scene. The 2026 release calendar — Heavencry , Citadelle , Chrome Tears , Featherfall , Together , When We Touch — operates at a cadence most producers can't sustain. Bio reads "Chxned to dysphoria"; the catalog backs the framing up. Appears on Angelcore: Compiled . Working start point: Featherfall as the solo demonstration, then Devotion for the collaboration context. Krembuur — 42K monthly listeners Krembuur sits at the slightly atmospheric-forward end of the scene's bigger middle layer. The catalog's most-streamed solo track is crying , at 177,723 plays — a clear demonstration of what the project does when the collaborators are not in the room. The 2026 EPs closer to truth and veil map the project's range cleanly: the first leans into deliberately quiet, vocally-textured work; the second pushes harder into the genre's atmosphere-forward register. The shared Devotion credit with Crisys and ProdChxn places Krembuur in the same collaboration triangle that anchors most of the working producers below the canonical tier's working catalog. Bio reads "Deadlock." Working start point: crying for the solo project, closer to truth for the most recent statement. Oyabe — 39K monthly listeners Oyabe is the scene's wider tier's most distinctly atmospheric producer. The bio — "Late night music ‧₊˚" — is exactly accurate; most of the catalog operates in the genre's dissolved, vocally-textured register, with structural patience that owes more to the ambient end of dance music than to its rhythmic center. The top track virtual memory at 317,883 plays is a collaboration with fervnt ; the solo work — Gave it all away , broken angel , Secrets — sits closer to the patient end of the catalog. Appears on multiple S4NCTUARY compilations (an adjacent imprint that handles thematic curations) plus Angelcore: Compiled . Working start point: virtual memory for the collaboration, Gave it all away for the solo register. fadevɇil — 58K monthly listeners fadevɇil operates with the broader roster's most aggressive catalog-building approach. The project's top track hyperdream sits at 765,525 plays — one of the highest individual track counts in the scene's working middle — and the catalog includes the p r a d a g i r l / p r a d a g i r l (Slowed) pair, both well above 200K plays each, demonstrating that the parallel-version distribution model is doing as much work for this project as it does for any of the canonical-tier releases. The aesthetic sits closer to the dreampop-leaning end of the angelcore spectrum, with vocal performances forward enough that some tracks read as legible songs rather than as pure mood pieces. Recent 2026 releases carbon , sextazy , and ultrarip demonstrate the project at its current center of gravity. Working start point: hyperdream for the breakout, then the p r a d a g i r l pair for the working method. fervnt — 85K monthly listeners fervnt is the broader producer pool's highest-streaming individual producer in this group. The top track umbra at 764,001 plays is comparable to fadevɇil's hyperdream as a satellite-tier breakout single. The catalog spans both the atmospheric register ( solace , digital warmth ) and the harder collaborative work ( virtual memory with Oyabe, make you cry as a multi-producer collaboration). The 2026 release cadence — blight , Angelie , plus continuing single releases — operates at the same dense pattern as the rest of the scene's bigger middle layer. The project also has the most diverse playlist placement footprint of the group: it sits on the main Angelcore curation, the Azurite Synthwave / Nightdrive Vibes playlist, the genre-specific Angelcore / Starly Type Songs editorial cut, and several others. Working start point: umbra for the breakout, virtual memory for the collaboration context. The Structural Pattern What these five producers demonstrate together is something useful about how the contemporary angelcore scene actually functions. The canonical tier (akiaura, LONOWN, DJ Anemia) does the work of setting the genre's working vocabulary and certifying its canonical tracks. The working producers below the canonical tier does the work of populating that vocabulary at a release cadence the canonical tier cannot sustain — and of doing so through collaborations dense enough that the resulting catalog reads as a single connected ecosystem rather than as a collection of isolated producers. For listeners arriving at the scene through any one of these producers — typically via the algorithm placing one of their tracks adjacent to an akiaura or LONOWN entry — the related-artist navigation does most of the work of building out the listening graph. Click through ProdChxn's "fans also like" and you arrive at Crisys, Krembuur, fervnt, and dxxm. Click through fervnt's and you arrive at Oyabe, ProdChxn, Crisys, and angelrot . The network's density is its functional value; no single producer in the scene's wider tier is the scene, but together they make the scene legible. — Further reading: a profile of Crisys , a profile of angelrot , the Azurite Records / EPSILE labels essay .

It sounds, vaguely, like a slowed-down rave song that got left in the rain. There are hi-hats but they sound like glass. There's a vocal but it's been pitched into something that doesn't belong to a body anymore. There's a kick drum but it's been wrapped in so much reverb it functions less like a beat and more like the memory of one. The genre signposts are all there — house tempo, electronic instrumentation, dance-music architecture — and yet the song refuses to operate as dance music. It is, structurally, mourning something. Probably itself. This essay is a working definition. Angelcore — like outsider house, hyperpop, or any other genre named retroactively by the internet — is not a fixed object.
